$comment: Every skill, agent and hook in the kit, the roles they serve, and the install profiles. Each agent names its model tier (kit/models.json): lint checks its file's model and effort against that tier, and the installer writes the same tier's model for every targeted tool; `sandbox: read-only` marks an agent that never writes, for tools that enforce it. A skill's or agent's role is the folder it lives in (kit/developer/ or kit/admin/); a hook's role is recorded here, because the hooks share one runtime folder. The installer reads this; `agent-setup lint` checks it against the tree. Profiles list skill names or @group; the `core` list is always installed, and so is every admin skill when the admin role is. Which skills are vendored (rebuilt from upstream, never hand-edited) is recorded in kit/vendor.json, not here.

roles.developer: What developers' agents use day to day: the domain skills, the delivery workflow, the review team and the guard hooks. Always installed.
roles.admin: Whoever sets the kit up and keeps it improving: sdlc-init, the enforcement audit, the learning loop and the session recorder. Its skills run only when invoked by name, so they cost developer sessions nothing. Installed unless --roles developer.

groups.domain: Engineering expertise, written for this kit: loads when the work matches the domain
groups.core: The delivery workflow — installed in every project
groups.design: UI build direction and real-browser verification — opt-in (--skills @design): the build-direction skill is ~22k tokens when it loads, and browser checks need a CLI on each machine
groups.admin: Setup, audit and the learning loop — the admin role

frontend.summary: UI components, pages, forms, client/server state, accessibility, frontend performance and tests

backend.summary: Domain logic, persistence, migrations, transactions, concurrency, jobs, caching, observability

api-design.summary: The middle layer: HTTP/GraphQL/gRPC contracts, BFFs, middleware, webhooks, third-party integrations

security.summary: Threat modelling, secure implementation, and security review of a change

architecture.summary: Boundaries, dependency rules, trade-off decisions and ADRs

design-system.summary: Tokens, theming, shared components, and the checks that keep UI on-system

agent-eval.summary: Evals for prompts, agents, LLM features and skills; baselines and regression gates

deliver.summary: The delivery cycle for larger or risky changes: brief, plan, build in verified steps, review, report

gates.summary: Run the repo's gates exactly as CI does, cheapest first, and report PASS/FAIL

ship-it.summary: Commit and open a PR the way this repo expects — never into production uninvited

handoff.summary: Write a precise handoff so the next session continues without re-deriving context

design-taste-frontend.summary: UI build direction: brief inference, design dials, anti-slop rules, pre-flight check

agent-browser.summary: Real-browser verification: screenshots, theme emulation, console, axe audit

sdlc-init.summary: Survey the repo; write its SDLC contract, knowledge base, overlays and gap register

self-improve.summary: Route captured lessons to where they are enforced; export kit improvements

enforcement-audit.summary: Audit what the repo claims against what it enforces; ranked gap register

scout.when: more than a handful of files to read: "where is…", "how does…", "what uses…"
scout.summary: Read-only exploration in its own context; returns a file:line map, not file contents

planner.when: M and L work, before the first edit; frontier for critical or cross-cutting change
planner.summary: Read-only: turns a brief into a plan of small, checkable steps — files, order, the test for each step, risks

implementer.when: a plan of more than a few edits, when you run above medium — one step per call
implementer.summary: Builds one plan step at a time, runs the step's check, returns what changed and the evidence

gate-runner.when: before a commit or PR, or when a full gate run would flood the conversation
gate-runner.summary: Runs the gates in its own context and returns MERGE-SAFE or BLOCKED

code-reviewer.when: a change across several files or layers, or a risky one — before calling it done
code-reviewer.summary: Read-only review of a diff against its brief: correctness, tests, scope; ranked findings

security-reviewer.when: auth, permissions, payments, personal data, uploads, webhooks, outbound calls, LLM tools; frontier where money or data loss is at stake
security-reviewer.summary: Read-only security review of a diff; ranked, evidenced findings

architecture-reviewer.when: a new module, dependency, service or datastore; a change across layers
architecture-reviewer.summary: Read-only boundary and dependency review of a change

doc-writer.when: any docs task beyond a line or two; one mechanical edit across many files
doc-writer.summary: Writes docs, the changelog and comments on a cheap model, and mechanical edits across files

docs-keeper.when: after a structural change, and before a release
docs-keeper.summary: Verifies .agents/docs claims against the tree and fixes drift

setup-clone.summary: Per clone: links the skills into .claude/skills for Claude Code (its session start runs it)

run-hook.summary: Runs the hooks in Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity and Windsurf, translating each agent's hook format

guard-git.summary: Denies production writes, force-pushes to shared branches, discarding uncommitted work and hook bypasses — naming the alternative

check-gates.summary: Runs the fast check an edit could have broken, right after the edit

stop-check.summary: Asks once for a check when the agent finishes with code changed after the last one, and for a review of risky work nobody reviewed

prompt-intake.summary: A large or risky request (auth, payments, data, production, secrets) → the agent writes a brief first; a docs task or a plan to build → the cheaper agent for it

context-budget.summary: Past the token budget: asks the agent to delegate and read narrowly, tells the person to /clear when the task is done, and points a cleared session to the handoff

branch-check.summary: Speaks at session start only when the branch needs attention: production, detached, stale, or a wrong config

session-eval.summary: Records one row of facts per context window, at no token cost

learning-signals.summary: Notes corrections for the learnings inbox, keeps a friction log, stops a command failing three times

standard.description: The general engineering skills and the delivery workflow.

web.description: Full-stack web product. UI build direction and browser verification are opt-in: --skills @design.

frontend.description: Frontend app or site. UI build direction and browser verification are opt-in: --skills @design.

ai-app.description: Product with LLM or agent features.
